extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators, research administrators, institutional officials, and NSF staff preparing or administering NSF proposals and awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory policy for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and administering proposals and NSF grants/cooperative agreements, including proposal format, merit review criteria, award conditions, financial and post-award requirements. Applies across NSF directorates unless modified by program solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit Review Principles (foundation for NSF proposal review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAPPG lists merit review principles as the overarching guidance for evaluating proposals; Program Officers and reviewers apply these principles in recommending awards. (Section referenced in Table of Contents; full principles provided in Part III.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual Merit (one of the Merit Review Criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a primary criterion for evaluating proposals under NSF's merit review process. The Project’s potential to advance knowledge is evaluated under this criterion. (Listed in Part III: Merit Review Criteria.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader Impacts (one of the Merit Review Criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a primary criterion for evaluating proposals under NSF's merit review process. The Project’s benefits to society, education, diversity, and broader impacts are evaluated under this criterion. (Listed in Part III: Merit Review Criteria.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with Instructions for Proposal Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must conform to the PAPPG instructions and any program solicitation modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAPPG requires strict conformance with its proposal preparation instructions (format, contents, page limits, etc.), except where a program solicitation explicitly modifies those provisions. Nonconforming proposals may be returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Format: Pagination, Margins and Spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Pagination Instructions and Proposal Margin and Spacing Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide prescribes pagination, margins, and spacing requirements for proposals; these formatting rules must be followed for proposal acceptance. (Detailed formatting instructions appear in Part I.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary must be included as part of the proposal contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary content and format requirements are specified as mandatory components of a proposal; reviewers and NSF staff use it to understand the project scope and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description (including Results from Prior NSF Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description must include the narrative of the proposed work and, where applicable, Results from Prior NSF Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Description is the main substantive narrative with page limitations and rules about including URLs; proposals that fail to include required prior support information may be deficient. (Page limitations and inclusion of URLs are noted in TOC.)

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: All relevant literature and prior work must be cited in the References Cited section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References provide context for Intellectual Merit and allow reviewers to assess novelty and foundation of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch(es) Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketches must include Professional Preparation, Appointments, Products, and Synergistic Activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biosketches must follow specified content elements (a–d) to allow reviewers to evaluate Investigators’ qualifications and track records; format and page limits are prescribed elsewhere in the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior and Other Personnel Roles and Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal must identify senior personnel and other personnel and include documentation of their roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on personnel is used to evaluate the Investigators criterion under merit review and to assess project staffing adequacy and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed budget and justification required, covering all cost categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets must itemize Salaries & Wages, Fringe Benefits, Equipment, Travel, Participant Support, Other Direct Costs (materials, publication, consultants, computer services, subawards), and justify the requested amounts per PAPPG rules; cost allowability is governed by Part II (Allowability of Costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Personnel Salaries & Wages Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy governing compensation for senior personnel included in budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAPPG specifies rules for charging salaries and person-months for senior personnel; proposals must follow these policies when requesting salary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and Clerical Salaries & Wages Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy restricting charging administrative and clerical salaries as direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/clerical costs are typically treated as indirect; charging them as direct costs requires meeting narrow criteria and documented justification per PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits must be budgeted and justified per institutional rates and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fringe benefit rates should be consistent with institutional rates and properly applied to salary lines in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and Capital Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment requests must be justified and conform to NSF definitions of equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment thresholds, title, use, and accountability are addressed in Part II (Title to Equipment, Property Management Standards). Requests should align with project needs and NSF policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel (Domestic and Foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel costs (domestic and foreign) must be reasonable, justified, and within policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate guidance exists for domestic vs foreign travel; international travel may have additional considerations (passports/visas, projects abroad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Support Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant support costs must be specifically identified and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant support (e.g., stipends, travel for workshop participants) has special budget treatment and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs — Materials, Publication, Consultant, Computer Services, Subawards
rubrics_metrics.description: Other direct cost categories must be itemized and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category (materials, dissemination, consultants, computing services, subawards) has examples and allowability guidance in the PAPPG; subawards require separate justification and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs (F&A) Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect (F&A) costs must follow NSF policy and negotiated rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs are charged per institution’s negotiated F&A rate unless special NSF policy applies; CAAR negotiates rates when NSF is the predominant funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of This Request and Total Direct and Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must state the Amount of This Request and calculate Total Direct and Indirect Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget summaries must accurately reflect the requested NSF funding and include all direct and indirect cost calculations per PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing — General and Mandatory Commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing policies, including mandatory cost sharing commitments and recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide explains when cost sharing is required, how commitments must be documented, and records kept; in general NSF discourages voluntary committed cost sharing unless required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of allowable and unallowable costs (examples: entertainment, meals and coffee breaks, alcoholic beverages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal budgets must avoid unallowable items and follow PAPPG guidance on allowable costs and conflicting guidelines; certain costs require prior written approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of current and pending support for senior personnel and key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on other support is required to assess commitment and avoid overlap/duplication; must follow PAPPG format and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of institutional facilities, equipment, and other resources available to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors use this section to evaluate project feasibility and environment; sufficient detail is required to judge capacity to perform the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Information and Supplementary Documentation / Appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for special information, supplementary documentation, and any appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices and supplementary materials are tightly controlled; only permitted material per PAPPG may be included and excess material may lead to return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Required institutional and PI certifications associated with proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications (e.g., conflict of interest, drug-free workplace, debarment) must be provided via the AOR and institutional officials as stipulated by the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Suggested Reviewers or Reviewers Not to Include
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may provide names of suggested reviewers and those they prefer not to review the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is advisory; Program Officers select reviewers. Conflicts of interest and potential bias should be considered when suggesting or excluding reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Submit Proposals — Categories of Proposers / Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible proposers include universities and colleges, nonprofit non-academic organizations, for-profit organizations, state and local governments, unaffiliated individuals, international organizations, and other federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is defined in Chapter I.F; proposers must check program solicitations for additional restrictions and follow organizational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Submissions and Special Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of submissions: Letters of Intent, Preliminary Proposals, Invite/Not Invite, Full Proposals, Rapid Response Research (RAPID), EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, Ideas Lab, FASED, Conferences, Equipment, Centers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each submission type has specific rules, deadlines, and requirements described in PAPPG and program solicitations; proposers must follow the mechanism-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Submit Proposals — Electronic Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission requirements via Research.gov and FastLane; DUNS, SAM, and NSF ID requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must meet NSF electronic submission rules and have required organizational registrations (DUNS/SAM); Grants.gov applicants must follow Grants.gov Application Guide when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Receipt, Deadlines and Special Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for proposal receipt, target dates, deadline dates, submission windows, and special exceptions (e.g., natural disasters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide defines deadlines, target dates, and process for exceptions (e.g., closures or disasters); late or incorrectly submitted proposals may not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, proposals must include Results from Prior NSF Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in Project Description for PIs who previously received NSF support; provides reviewers with track record and outcomes information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative and Group Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing collaborative/group proposals, including multi-institution submissions and governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative proposals must follow PAPPG guidance on submission format, budget roles (subawards vs consortium), and responsibilities of lead and partner organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals Involving Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional requirements and approvals for proposals involving vertebrate animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such proposals require documentation of animal care and use committee (IACUC) approvals and justification per PAPPG and applicable laws/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional requirements and IRB approvals for proposals involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human subjects research must comply with Federal regulations and institutional IRB requirements, with documentation described in PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and disclosure requirements for research that could be dual-use (DURC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must follow NSF policies on DURC and provide required information and mitigation plans if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects Requiring High-Performance Computing, Large Data Storage, or Advanced Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Special instructions for projects needing significant HPC, storage, or visualization resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must document resource needs, availability, and justification; may trigger additional review or coordination with facility providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Prior Approval Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior written approvals required for certain pre- and post-award actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific actions (e.g., budget reallocations, rebudgeting beyond thresholds, changes in scope or key personnel) may require prior NSF approval as detailed in Part II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers and Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Officers select reviewers; reviewers are subject matter experts and provide merit review that informs award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers recommend which projects should be funded; PIs receive unattributed verbatim copies of peer reviews; selection procedures and confidentiality rules are defined in Part III.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Award Types and Distinctions (Grant, Continuing Grant, Cost Reimbursement, Fixed Amount Award, Cooperative Agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and distinctions between types of NSF awards including standard grant, continuing grant, cost reimbursement award, fixed amount award, and cooperative agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each award type has different expectations for agency involvement, accountability, and administration; cooperative agreements imply substantial NSF involvement and separate conditions; proposers/awardees must understand implications for administration and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Responsibilities and NSF-Grantee Relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are responsible for conducting project activities and managing funds; NSF provides specified support and monitors compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantee obligations include prudent fund management, performance of project as proposed, and compliance with award terms; NSF monitors progress and enforces requirements including suspension/termination if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring Project Performance and Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring, annual project reports, final project report, and Project Outcomes Report for the General Public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must submit regular technical and financial reports per award conditions; public-facing outcomes reporting is required to communicate results to a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Financial Management and Payment Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial management standards, payment requirements, requesting payments, and payment policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must maintain financial systems consistent with Federal standards; policies cover advances, reimbursements, working capital advances, and final disbursement reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property and Title to Equipment Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Title to equipment and property management standards (differences for non-profit and for-profit organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules govern acquisition, title, use, accountability, and disposition of equipment purchased with NSF funds; special rules apply when title is retained by NSF or for different organization types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records Retention and Audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for retention of records and audit readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must retain records and be prepared for audits; CAAR and DGA oversee cost/audit resolution and financial review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Discrimination and Civil Rights Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with Title VI, Section 504, Title IX, Age Discrimination Act, and E.O. 11246 EEO requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and awardees must adhere to federal nondiscrimination statutes and equal employment opportunity obligations as explained in Part II.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Considerations and Travel to Foreign Countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on travel to foreign countries, projects abroad, passports/visas, charter flights, and related international considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International activities have special logistical, legal, and policy implications; proposers must document and justify foreign activities and follow applicable rules and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Information and Release of Proposal/Grantee Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for handling confidential/proprietary information, questionnaires, and release of information by NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietary or privileged information should be identified; NSF follows FOIA and other statutes in releasing information; guidance on marking and processing proprietary material is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Administration Disputes, Suspension, Termination and Misconduct Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for suspension/termination, dispute resolution, and reporting possible research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAPPG describes suspension/termination definitions and procedures, informal resolution methods, and responsibilities for reporting research misconduct; OIG contact information is provided for allegations of misconduct, fraud, waste, or abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Roles and Responsibilities (Program Officers, Division Directors, DGA, DIAS, DACS, DFM, LFO, OGC, ODI, OIG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of NSF offices and their responsibilities relevant to proposal review, award issuance, policy, financial management, legal counsel, diversity, and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding which NSF office handles particular aspects (policy, award issuance, audits, legal issues, diversity/civil rights, large facilities, etc.) helps proposers and awardees navigate procedures and contacts for questions or issues.
